instruction: Merge every PDF attached to the 'Paper Recommendation' email in Thunderbird into one valid PDF file named attachment_full.pdf, then upload it to Google Drive.

query: title = 'attachment_full.pdf' and trashed = false and 'root' in parents

metadata.explanation: Variation checks PDF file integrity with partial credit scoring: 40% for valid PDF structure (not corrupted), 30% for sufficient pages (at least 50 pages), 30% for readable text content. The gold PDF has 75 pages with extractable text. This ensures the merge operation produced a well-formed, readable document.

llm_judge_reasons: CORRECTION: Previous judgment incorrectly flagged metric lines 54-56. The actual logic at lines 57-59 correctly preserves partial credit - it only returns 0.0 when score==0.0 (no valid structure AND no pages AND no text), not when score>0. A valid PDF with 50+ pages but no text correctly scores 0.7.

Improved text verification: Getter now samples multiple pages (first, last, middle, quarter, three-quarter pages) instead of just page 0, providing more comprehensive text detection for the 75-page merged PDF.
Partial credit correctly implemented: Metric awards 0.4 for valid structure, 0.3 for page count, 0.3 for text. These are cumulative and preserved correctly.

Minor limitation: Evaluator cannot verify that PDFs were actually merged from Thunderbird 'Paper Recommendation' email attachments. It only validates the final PDF properties (valid, 50+ pages, readable text). Could theoretically pass with any qualifying PDF uploaded to Google Drive.
Minor limitation: Text sampling of 5 pages out of 75 may miss edge cases, but is reasonable for practical verification that the PDF has extractable text content.
Static validation warning about type (Any) vs (Dict) is a false positive - the metric correctly handles expected as the rules dict per framework convention.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Add more comprehensive text checking by calculating total text length across all sampled pages and requiring minimum character threshold (e.g., >1000 chars) to ensure substantial text content.
Optional enhancement: Consider checking PDF metadata (creation date, modification date) to verify recent creation, though this is not foolproof as metadata can be manipulated.
Documentation clarification: Add comment explaining that evaluator verifies final PDF properties but cannot trace the merge operation from Thunderbird email attachments.
